# The Sector Debrief

> Honest conversations on humanitarian and development work. A podcast hosted by Ali Al Mokdad, Kim Kucinskas, and Thomas Jepson-Lay.

The Sector Debrief is the real conversations that shape the humanitarian and development world. The ones that usually happen when the microphones are off. The show talks openly about political shifts, shrinking budgets, power dynamics, localization of aid, civil society, and the future of crisis response.

## Hosts

- Ali Al Mokdad. Humanitarian operations and leadership practitioner. Worked across Save the Children International, Danish Refugee Council, International Medical Corps, CARE, ACF, NRC, and Geneva Call. Field experience in South Sudan, Bangladesh, Syria, Niger, Afghanistan, and elsewhere. Currently in Copenhagen.
- Kim Kucinskas. Humanitarian leadership and transformation work.
- Thomas Jepson-Lay. Humanitarian sector practitioner and critic of institutional defaults.

## Where to listen

- YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@TheSectorDebrief
- Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/show/1igMsRaLcEY9DN64GBDKbW
- Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1861790994

## Episodes

- [Episode 7: Donations, Collaboration, and AI in the Room](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vPJAWTb2dPI) (27 May 2026, 54 min). A Sunday-morning donation knock turns into a wider conversation on social contract versus funding problem, AI in the workplace (productivity gains clawed back, skill atrophy, agents that do not collaborate with each other), and collaboration as a discipline rather than a slogan.
- [Episode 6: The Sector Is Changing. How Do You Make Sense Of It?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7w_FXEcBzs4) (7 May 2026, 51 min). Civil society in transition. What is civil society for, and why are people no longer experiencing it as a public good. Not just a funding problem, a social contract problem.
- [Episode 5: Who Are You in the Room, Identity vs Positionality, and Leadership in Times of Disruption](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bv47XLE50hw) with Aisha Tambajang (29 Mar 2026, 52 min). Ancestral responsibility, values-based leadership, "rushing to fix" versus "curiosity to solve," headquarters versus field tensions.
- [Episode 4: The CEO Perspective, Urgent Patience, and Why Idealism Is Not Naivety](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qNM0NWeZ4fA) with Sofia Sprechmann Sineiro, former Secretary General of CARE International (7 Mar 2026, 58 min). Pragmatic optimism, locally led development, balancing authenticity with institutional survival.
- [Episode 3: Humanitarian Leadership Under Pressure, Identity vs Strategy, and What Comes Next](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nQpnWvOoEio) (7 Feb 2026, 46 min). Pressurized humanitarian systems, grassroots innovation versus institutional survival mode, organizational sustainability during transformation.
- [Episode 2: What Does Sector Mean, Leadership Tension, and Change](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VVe2TM2z5UI) (19 Jan 2026, 49 min). What "sector" terminology actually encompasses, humanitarian diplomacy, escalating leadership friction.
- [Episode 1: What This Space Is About, Leadership and Reflections](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FqxeBin5bbQ) (13 Dec 2025, 38 min). The inaugural episode. The opening note: this won't be a polished podcast. It will be honest.

## Themes the show returns to

- Localization of aid and decision-making power
- Funding cuts and what the sector does next
- Leadership values under institutional pressure
- Headquarters versus field dynamics
- Identity, positionality, and who holds the floor in humanitarian rooms
- The social contract between aid organisations and the publics they claim to serve
